title: Developer Experience Docs: SDK Guides, Quickstarts, API Examples, Ops & Canonical Fixes
author: Aisha Patel
summary: This document defines the standards, templates, operating procedures, and canonical fixes for Developer Experience (DevEx) documentation: SDK guides, quickstarts & templates, API examples, docs site operations, and the top support issues. It centralizes ownership, publishing workflows, and troubleshooting steps used by DevEx, SDK, and Support teams.
purpose: Provide a single, actionable reference to produce consistent, high-quality DevEx documentation that reduces developer onboarding time, lowers support volume, and speeds iteration on SDKs and examples.
scope: Applies to all DevEx-authored content maintained in the confluence/eng-developer-experience area: SDK guides, quickstarts, templates, API examples, docs site operating procedures, and canonical support fixes. Does not apply to product PRDs or internal engineering RFCs unless they include public SDK reference material.
roles_and_responsibilities:
- DevEx Documentation Owners: maintain templates, review PRs, and triage publishing issues.
- SDK Owners: keep language SDK guides up to date with code/API changes.
- Support (Tier 1/2): escalate recurring issues to DevEx and add canonical fixes.
- Docs Site Platform: owns CI, build pipeline, and runtime (Netlify/Docs platform) availability.
- Product/Platform: provide API changelog and migration notes.
Ownership: DevEx (primary), SDK teams (secondary), Support (input). On-call channel: #devex-docs (Slack).
standards_and_naming_conventions:
File name convention: lowercase, dash-separated, short descriptive, end with year if time-bounded (e.g. sdk-python-quickstart-2026.json).
Page titles: short human-readable title + year if applicable.
Section order for guides: Summary -> When to use -> Quickstart -> Examples -> Troubleshooting -> Versioning -> Related pages.
Code snippets: always include working copy/paste examples for latest stable SDK and a minimal curl REST example.
API examples must include: endpoint, method, request headers, minimal request body, expected success response and common error responses.
Labels: 3–6 tags at creation.
Confidentiality: default to internal unless approved by legal/security for external release.
sdk_guides:
Guidelines for SDK guides:
- Purpose: explain idiomatic usage, configuration, and common patterns for each language SDK.
- Structure: Intro, Installation, Auth, Basic Example, Advanced Patterns (retry/backoff, streaming, pagination), Troubleshooting, Migration Notes, Release Notes link.
- Versioning: include 'Last tested with' line (SDK version + API version).
- Test matrix: document which runtime and OS combinations are validated.
- Example:
  - Python minimal example:
    ```python
    from redwood import RedwoodClient
    client = RedwoodClient(api_key="${REDWOOD_API_KEY}")
    resp = client.chat.create(model="rw-instruct-1", messages=[{"role":"user","content":"Hello"}])
    print(resp.output_text)
    ```
- Linting: run 'docs-lint' and 'code-exec' checks as part of PR.
- Ownership: SDK team must update within 7 days of breaking API changes or deprecations.
quickstarts_and_templates:
Quickstarts should be focused, copy/paste runnable, and under 10–15 minutes to follow. Templates available in repository: /repos/devex/docs-templates.
Recommended quickstart types:
1) Hello world (3–5 minute): minimal auth + single API call.
2) Chat integration (10 minute): streaming + function calling example.
3) Embeddings + similarity search (10 minute): index pipeline.
4) Deployment example: Dedicated & Private quickstart (ops checklist + sample config).
Provided templates: PR template for docs, API example template (includes req/resp table), troubleshooting template, release note template.
Quickstart checklist (author to verify before publish):
- [ ] Copy/paste runnable in 5 minutes
- [ ] Tests pass in docs CI
- [ ] Contains minimal security guidance (avoid printing secrets)
- [ ] Includes expected outputs and screenshots where applicable
api_examples:
API examples must include both SDK and raw HTTP (curl) forms. Example for chat.create (curl):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat.create \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"rw-instruct-1","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Summarize the following..."}]}'
```
Each example should document: endpoint, supported params, rate limits (if applicable), typical latency, and caveats (streaming vs non-streaming). Maintain a short 'Common Errors' table for each endpoint, e.g.:
| HTTP Code | Condition | Recommended action |
|---|---|---|
| 401 | Invalid API key | Check env var and token scope |
| 422 | Unsupported model or bad payload | Validate model id / request schema |
| 503 | Transient capacity error | Retry with exponential backoff, fallback model |
docs_site_operating_procedures:
Docs site operating procedures (daily/weekly/monthly):
Daily:
- Check docs CI: green builds in <30 minutes.
- Monitor broken links and search indexing errors.
Weekly:
- Review top 10 search queries and update landing/quickstarts.
- Triage incoming doc-related support tickets labeled 'docs'.
Monthly:
- Run 'doc smoke tests' across SDK quickstarts for each supported language.
- Audit top support issues and ensure canonical fixes are present.
Incident playbook (docs site outage):
1) Triage in #devex-docs and #infra-ops.
2) Rollback last docs site deploy if a build/regression is suspected.
3) If build system failing, trigger manual publish from stable artifact.
4) Postmortem within 72 hours if outage >15 minutes.
CI & Publishing notes:
- Docs are built by 'docs-ci' pipeline; PRs must pass spellcheck, lint, code-exec.
- Stable publishing cadence: weekly for minor updates, ad-hoc for critical fixes.
- Hotfix process: tag release 'docs-hotfix' and run manual deploy job.
top_support_issues_and_canonical_fixes:
This section lists the top recurring developer support issues encountered in 2025–2026 and the canonical fixes included in docs. Update this table when a new recurring issue is identified.
1) Auth failures (wrong scope / expired key): canonical fix: add explicit examples for setting env var, confirm token scopes and show test curl.
2) Model mismatch errors: canonical fix: maintain 'models supported' table and migration guide; add runtime detection to examples.
3) Streaming timeouts: canonical fix: recommend client-side keepalive, adjust server-side timeout guidance, and provide reconnect examples.
4) Large request payloads (rate limits / memory): canonical fix: document chunking approach and recommended batch sizes; include server-side error handling.
5) Confusing error codes: canonical fix: expand 'Common Errors' with clear actionable steps and links to debugging tools.
Canonical fix lifecycle: Support files a ticket labeled 'docs-canonical-fix' -> DevEx triages within 3 business days -> Author updates doc and tests -> Publish with changelog entry.
publishing_and_release_process:
Steps to publish or update DevEx docs:
1) Create branch using docs-<short-desc>-YYYYMMDD.
2) Open PR against main with checklists filled (see templates).
3) Automated checks run (lint, spellcheck, code-exec, link-check).
4) Reviewer from DevEx + SDK owner must approve.
5) Merge triggers docs-ci; verify staging site then promote to stable.
6) If change affects SDK behavior, coordinate a cross-team slack ping to #platform-sdk and include a migration snippet.
Rollback criteria and steps:
- If post-deploy regression or build failure, open an incident with tag 'docs-deploy' and rollback to previous stable tag using the 'promote' job.
Metrics and KPIs to track impact:
- Search satisfaction (top 10 queries resolved)
- Time-to-first-success for quickstarts (target <10 minutes)
- Docs-related support ticket volume (target -20% YoY after improvements)
